cards.method_and_execution: I helped shape the tracking and estimation workflow around the decisions teams make, not around more dashboards. It showed when people actually saw an offer, let teams change assumptions, and clearly split approved budget, expected rewards, rewards used, and actual cost.
cards.artifacts: Requirements, data definitions, and a workflow for local teams.
cards.impact_or_learning: I learned that a trustworthy tool must show how fresh its data is and what it assumes. Otherwise it just automates the same confusion that slowed down the manual work.

cards.title: Planning capacity for member eligibility checks
reach_out_when: You need to match eligibility demand with operational capacity
You want to avoid decisions based on out-of-date usage figures
cards.trigger: Some members had to be verified as eligible before they could join. Those checks had limited capacity.
cards.problem: Demand forecasts existed, but we did not yet know how much capacity was being used or how well the checks were working.
cards.method_and_execution: I gathered demand inputs and set up two ways to forecast: one for a growing member group and one for a shrinking one. I held back a recommendation until current usage was confirmed.
cards.artifacts: A capacity tracker, a forecast model, and a simple decision guide.
cards.impact_or_learning: I learned that planning for member eligibility has to combine demand, sign-up rates, current usage, and how the checks actually run. Projecting from member numbers alone is not enough.

cards.title: Field research on how drivers use connected-car services
reach_out_when: You need to find unmet needs before designing a mobility service
You need to turn field research into product questions
cards.trigger: I worked on research into how drivers used their vehicles and digital services in everyday life.
cards.problem: Ideas for new features needed to be based on drivers' real motivations, habits, and frustrations, which usual product assumptions could miss.
cards.method_and_execution: I helped design research that combined observing drivers with interviews. I then helped organise the findings around behaviours, attitudes, and unmet needs. I turned what we heard into questions for designing services, while being clear that the sample was small.
cards.artifacts: Interview guides, fieldwork summaries, customer journey maps, and insight decks.
cards.impact_or_learning: I learned that this kind of research is most useful when it changes the questions a product team asks. It should spark ideas to test, not stand in for the whole market.

cards.title: Mapping research partnerships between India and Japan
reach_out_when: You need to map a research ecosystem
You need to find practical barriers to international collaboration
cards.trigger: I contributed to a study of opportunities for joint research and startup support between India and Japan.
cards.problem: The study needed a comparable picture of institutions, how they already worked together, and what got in the way. A simple directory of organisations would not do.
cards.method_and_execution: I helped organise desk research and interviews into a map of potential partners, existing collaboration, and practical issues. We separated documented activity from opportunities that would need to be checked directly.
cards.artifacts: An institution map, interview notes, research reports, and an executive summary.
cards.impact_or_learning: I learned that these studies are most useful when they link the landscape to specific partnership questions and show where the evidence is thin.

cards.title: Benchmarking battery suppliers
reach_out_when: You need to compare suppliers on more than price
You need a structured approach to a major sourcing decision
cards.trigger: An industrial client was considering a more coordinated way to buy batteries.
cards.problem: Choosing suppliers meant weighing supply capacity, terms, delivery record, and strategic fit.
cards.method_and_execution: I assessed supplier and competitor information and helped draft a sourcing plan with criteria for choosing and negotiating with vendors.
cards.artifacts: A supplier assessment, a benchmark, sourcing options, and proposal material.
cards.impact_or_learning: I learned that a sourcing recommendation is stronger when it shows the trade-offs and assumptions behind the shortlist.

cards.title: Sales and service playbook for a luxury car brand
reach_out_when: You need a consistent high-end dealership experience
You need to turn customer expectations into clear steps for staff
cards.trigger: A luxury automotive brand wanted every customer to get the same experience.
cards.problem: The process had to cover everything from the first enquiry to after the sale, while meeting premium service expectations.
cards.method_and_execution: I researched what customers expected and helped write step-by-step sales procedures for the luxury customer journey.
cards.artifacts: A customer study, a journey map, sales procedures, and rollout guidance.
cards.impact_or_learning: I learned that a service standard works when its steps can be observed and frontline staff back it.

cards.title: Consulting proposals and client account management
reach_out_when: You need a repeatable consulting proposal process
You need to organise account opportunities and past-project knowledge
cards.trigger: Alongside project work, the consulting team needed to win new work and keep client relationships strong.
cards.problem: Proposals had to be tailored and on time, and past work had to be easy to reuse without making every pitch generic.
cards.method_and_execution: I wrote proposals and sales material, coordinated client accounts, and set up a more organised way to reuse past work when writing proposals.
cards.artifacts: Proposals, credentials, client briefs, a knowledge library, and trackers.
cards.impact_or_learning: I learned that winning work is easier when evidence of past delivery is easy to find and each proposal stays specific to the client.
